You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test case `testLongLineChunkingIndentIgnored` exercises the wrapping and indentation functionality of `HelpFormatter.printHelp`. The test provides a very narrow width (22 characters) and expects that long text, including option descriptions, is wrapped correctly with indentation.

From the current bug report and the test, there is a symptom of an infinite loop or OutOfMemoryError happening when wrapping words that don't fit into a line.

The key function responsible for wrapping text is `HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText`, which attempts to repeatedly find wrap positions in the input text and append wrapped lines to a StringBuffer. The method uses a loop and calls `findWrapPos` to find where to break lines.

Looking closely at `renderWrappedText`:
- At line 834, the text is updated by adding padding and trimming the remaining text after the wrap position.
- At line 835, the next wrap position `pos` is found.
- At lines 837-841, if no more wrap position (`pos == -1`), the text is appended and function returns normally.
- There is also a check at line 844-847 that appears to deal with a special case, possibly a safeguard to avoid infinite loops by forcing a break if wrap position is just before the padding.

From the current bug report's test:
When there is not enough space to display a single word on a line (a single long word with no spaces wider than the allowed width), `findWrapPos` might fail to find a proper wrap position (it returns -1 under some conditions). However, in `renderWrappedText`, the text is always trimmed and padded, but the code doesn't seem to handle properly the case when the word itself cannot be broken.

Looking at `findWrapPos`:
- It first tries to find newline or tab within the width; if found, returns it.
- If the line end is beyond text length, returns -1 (means no wrapping needed).
- It tries to find the last whitespace before width.
- If not found, it scans forward to find the first whitespace after width.
- If nothing found (end of string reached), returns -1.

Main problem occurs when there is a single long word longer than width with no whitespace character: `findWrapPos` will not find a break position and return -1.

Back in `renderWrappedText`, if `findWrapPos` returns -1 the first time (line 814-819), it appends the trimmed text and returns normally - no infinite loop there.

BUT inside the while(true) loop starting line 832:
- The text is prefixed with padding spaces plus trimmed substring starting at previous wrap position.
- Then calls findWrapPos again.
- If no wrap position is found, it appends and returns.
- But if a wrap position is found exactly at `nextLineTabStop - 1` (one less than the width), it forces the wrap position to width (line 844-847).

The problematic infinite loop appears because of padding plus `text.substring(pos)` trimming and wrapping calculations after the initial wrap.

In the failing test, the option description line is wrapped into multiple lines with indentation (descPad = 5). The first split appears fine but the subsequent trimmed strings in the infinite loop can still have the problematic word exceeding the width.

If `findWrapPos` keeps returning the same wrap position or fails to find a position that leads to progress in shortening the string (due to only padding and not properly breaking long words), the loop never exits.

In conclusion, the infinite loop is caused by `renderWrappedText` not properly handling the edge case when a single word is longer than the line width and there is padding (indentation). The `findWrapPos` method is unable to find a break position on that long word, leading to a situation where the same substring is used repeatedly in the infinite loop without shortening the remainder.

The bug is in the wrapping logic around `renderWrappedText` and `findWrapPos`, specifically how very long words are handled during wrapping with indentation.

The recent bug reports about ordering of options and command line parsing do not seem related to this wrapping and infinite loop issue. The current bug report and failing test sufficiently clarify the root cause.

# Next steps
Inspect and fix the logic in `HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText` and/or `HelpFormatter.findWrapPos` to break long words forcibly when no whitespace break is found to prevent infinite loops on very long words exceeding width.
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText(java.lang.StringBuffer,int,int,java.lang.String)
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.findWrapPos(java.lang.String,int,int)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
